system.overview: BART is a heavy rail rapid transit system serving the San Francisco Bay Area in California. It connects San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, and surrounding East Bay cities with lines extending to San Francisco International Airport and the Silicon Valley.

history.title: System Opens
history.description: BART opens with the first segment between Oakland and Fremont, becoming the first new rapid transit system in the United States since 1907.

history.title: Transbay Tube Opens
history.description: The Transbay Tube opens, connecting San Francisco to the East Bay through a tunnel beneath San Francisco Bay.

history.title: SFO Extension Opens
history.description: BART extends to San Francisco International Airport, providing direct rail access to the major regional airport.

history.title: Oakland Airport Connector
history.description: The Oakland Airport Connector opens, providing automated people mover service from Coliseum station to Oakland International Airport.

history.title: Warm Springs Extension
history.description: BART opens the Warm Springs/South Fremont station, the first phase of the Silicon Valley extension.

history.title: Milpitas and Berryessa Open
history.description: BART extends into Santa Clara County with new stations at Milpitas and Berryessa/North San Jose.

red.name: Richmond-Millbrae
red.description: The Red Line connects Richmond in the East Bay to Millbrae on the Peninsula, passing through downtown Oakland and San Francisco via the Transbay Tube.

yellow.name: Antioch-SFO/Millbrae
yellow.description: The Yellow Line provides service from Antioch in eastern Contra Costa County to San Francisco International Airport and Millbrae, serving the East Bay hills communities.

blue.name: Dublin/Pleasanton-Daly City
blue.description: The Blue Line connects the Tri-Valley area in the East Bay to Daly City on the Peninsula, serving downtown Oakland and San Francisco.

green.name: Berryessa-Daly City
green.description: The Green Line extends BART service to Silicon Valley, connecting Berryessa/North San Jose to Daly City through the Fremont corridor.

orange.name: Richmond-Berryessa
orange.description: The Orange Line provides a direct connection between Richmond and Silicon Valley, running through downtown Oakland and the Fremont corridor.

beige.name: Oakland Airport Connector
beige.description: The Oakland Airport Connector is an automated people mover connecting the Coliseum BART station to Oakland International Airport.

12th-street-oakland.name: 12th Street/Oakland City Center
12th-street-oakland.description: 12th Street is a major transfer station in downtown Oakland, serving as a hub for multiple BART lines and AC Transit buses.

16th-street-mission.name: 16th Street Mission
16th-street-mission.description: 16th Street Mission serves San Francisco's vibrant Mission District, known for its Latino culture, murals, and restaurants.

19th-street-oakland.name: 19th Street/Oakland
19th-street-oakland.description: 19th Street serves the Uptown and Lake Merritt neighborhoods of Oakland, near the Paramount Theatre and Fox Oakland Theatre.

24th-street-mission.name: 24th Street Mission
24th-street-mission.description: 24th Street Mission is the southern end of BART service in the Mission District, near the historic Balmy Alley murals.

antioch.name: Antioch
antioch.description: Antioch is the eastern terminus of the Yellow Line, served by eBART diesel trains connecting to electric BART at Pittsburg/Bay Point.

ashby.name: Ashby
ashby.description: Ashby station serves South Berkeley and is home to one of the Bay Area's largest weekend flea markets in its parking lot.

balboa-park.name: Balboa Park
balboa-park.description: Balboa Park is a major transfer point between BART and Muni Metro, with adjacent bus connections and a park-and-ride facility.

bay-fair.name: Bay Fair
bay-fair.description: Bay Fair is a junction station where the Dublin/Pleasanton and Fremont lines diverge, named after the nearby Bayfair Center mall.

berryessa.name: Berryessa/North San Jose
berryessa.description: Berryessa is the current southern terminus of BART's Silicon Valley extension, with plans to extend further to downtown San Jose.

castro-valley.name: Castro Valley
castro-valley.description: Castro Valley station serves the unincorporated community of Castro Valley in the East Bay hills.

civic-center.name: Civic Center/UN Plaza
civic-center.description: This station serves San Francisco's Civic Center, City Hall, and numerous government buildings.

entrances.name: A3 1150 Market Street - UN Plaza Stairs

coliseum.name: Coliseum
coliseum.description: Coliseum station serves the Oakland Coliseum complex and provides connections to the Oakland Airport via the Oakland Airport Connector.

entrances.name: Elevated Walkway to Amtrak Station, Coliseum Arena

colma.name: Colma
colma.description: Colma station serves the town of Colma and nearby shopping centers, with large park-and-ride facilities.

concord.name: Concord
concord.description: Concord station serves the city of Concord with extensive parking and bus connections to surrounding communities.

daly-city.name: Daly City
daly-city.address: 500 John Daly Blvd, Daly City, CA 94014
daly-city.description: Daly City is the terminus for Blue and Green lines and a major transfer point, with extensive parking facilities serving commuters from the Peninsula.

entrances.name: A John Daly, Junipero Serra Blvd
B De Long St, St Charles Ave

downtown-berkeley.name: Downtown Berkeley
downtown-berkeley.description: Downtown Berkeley station serves the city's vibrant downtown area and the University of California, Berkeley campus.

dublin-pleasanton.name: Dublin/Pleasanton
dublin-pleasanton.description: Dublin/Pleasanton is the eastern terminus of the Blue Line with extensive parking and connections to ACE commuter rail.

el-cerrito-del-norte.name: El Cerrito del Norte
el-cerrito-del-norte.description: El Cerrito del Norte is a major bus transfer point with extensive parking, serving as a gateway for riders from western Contra Costa County.

el-cerrito-plaza.name: El Cerrito Plaza
el-cerrito-plaza.description: El Cerrito Plaza station is adjacent to the El Cerrito Plaza shopping center and serves central El Cerrito.

embarcadero.name: Embarcadero
embarcadero.description: Embarcadero is a major transit hub in San Francisco's Financial District, adjacent to the Ferry Building and providing connections to Muni Metro and buses.

fremont.name: Fremont
fremont.description: Fremont station is a major transit hub in the southern East Bay, with extensive park-and-ride facilities.

fruitvale.name: Fruitvale
fruitvale.description: Fruitvale station is known for its award-winning transit village development and serves the diverse Fruitvale neighborhood.

glen-park.name: Glen Park
glen-park.description: Glen Park station serves the Glen Park neighborhood and is the last underground station before BART emerges to the surface heading south.

hayward.name: Hayward
hayward.description: Hayward station serves downtown Hayward and is a major bus transfer point for AC Transit routes serving the East Bay.

lafayette.name: Lafayette
lafayette.description: Lafayette station serves the suburban community of Lafayette with extensive park-and-ride facilities in the Lamorinda area.

lake-merritt.name: Lake Merritt
lake-merritt.description: Lake Merritt station serves Oakland's Chinatown, the Oakland Museum of California, and the scenic Lake Merritt area.

entrances.name: B1 NW 8th & Oak St Jack London Sq

macarthur.name: MacArthur
macarthur.description: MacArthur is a major transfer station where the Richmond and Pittsburg/Bay Point lines diverge, with transit-oriented development nearby.

millbrae.name: Millbrae
millbrae.description: Millbrae is an intermodal station providing connections to Caltrain commuter rail service to San Jose and the Peninsula.

milpitas.name: Milpitas
milpitas.description: Milpitas station is part of BART's Silicon Valley extension, providing connections to VTA light rail and bus services.

montgomery-street.name: Montgomery Street
montgomery-street.description: Montgomery Street station serves the heart of San Francisco's Financial District and provides connections to Muni Metro.

north-berkeley.name: North Berkeley
north-berkeley.description: North Berkeley station serves the residential neighborhoods of northern Berkeley with substantial park-and-ride facilities.

north-concord-martinez.name: North Concord/Martinez
north-concord-martinez.description: North Concord/Martinez station serves northern Concord and provides the closest BART access for Martinez residents.

oakland-airport.name: Oakland International Airport
oakland-airport.description: Oakland Airport station is the terminus of the automated Oakland Airport Connector, providing direct service to both airport terminals.

orinda.name: Orinda
orinda.description: Orinda station serves the affluent Lamorinda communities and is the first station after the Berkeley Hills tunnel heading east.

pittsburg-center.name: Pittsburg Center
pittsburg-center.description: Pittsburg Center is part of the eBART diesel multiple unit extension, serving downtown Pittsburg.

pittsburg-bay-point.name: Pittsburg/Bay Point
pittsburg-bay-point.description: Pittsburg/Bay Point station serves eastern Contra Costa County with massive parking facilities and is the transfer point to eBART.

pleasant-hill.name: Pleasant Hill/Contra Costa Centre
pleasant-hill.description: Pleasant Hill station is surrounded by transit-oriented development and serves as a hub for central Contra Costa County commuters.

powell-street.name: Powell Street
powell-street.description: Powell Street is one of the busiest stations in the system, serving Union Square and providing connections to the famous San Francisco cable cars.

richmond.name: Richmond
richmond.description: Richmond is the northern terminus of the Red and Orange lines, providing connections to Amtrak Capitol Corridor service.

rockridge.name: Rockridge
rockridge.description: Rockridge station serves the upscale Rockridge neighborhood of Oakland, known for its restaurants and boutique shopping along College Avenue.

san-bruno.name: San Bruno
san-bruno.description: San Bruno station is a junction point where trains split between the SFO Airport branch and the Millbrae mainline.

sfo-airport.name: San Francisco International Airport
sfo-airport.address: SFO International Terminal, San Francisco, CA 94128
sfo-airport.description: SFO Airport station provides direct rail access to San Francisco International Airport, the busiest airport in Northern California.

san-leandro.name: San Leandro
san-leandro.address: 1401 San Leandro Blvd, San Leandro, CA 94577
san-leandro.description: San Leandro station serves downtown San Leandro and the surrounding residential areas with extensive parking.

south-hayward.name: South Hayward
south-hayward.description: South Hayward station serves southern Hayward and Union City residents with substantial park-and-ride facilities.

south-san-francisco.name: South San Francisco
south-san-francisco.address: 1333 Mission Rd, South San Francisco, CA 94080
south-san-francisco.description: South San Francisco station serves the biotech corridor and provides access to the industrial heart of South San Francisco.

union-city.name: Union City
union-city.description: Union City station is an intermodal hub with connections to the Altamont Corridor Express (ACE) commuter rail to the Central Valley.

walnut-creek.name: Walnut Creek
walnut-creek.address: 200 Ygnacio Valley Rd, Walnut Creek, CA 94596
walnut-creek.description: Walnut Creek station serves the major commercial center of central Contra Costa County with large parking structures.

warm-springs.name: Warm Springs/South Fremont
warm-springs.description: Warm Springs station serves southern Fremont and the growing tech employment centers near Tesla's factory.

west-dublin-pleasanton.name: West Dublin/Pleasanton
west-dublin-pleasanton.description: West Dublin/Pleasanton station serves the commercial and residential growth areas between Dublin and Pleasanton.

west-oakland.name: West Oakland
west-oakland.description: West Oakland station is a key connection point for Transbay service, where trains heading to San Francisco converge before crossing the bay.

railcars.name: A Car (Original Fleet)
railcars.description: The original A Cars were the first fleet of BART vehicles, featuring a distinctive space-age design. They served the system for over 50 years before being replaced by the Fleet of the Future.

railcars.name: B Car (Expansion Fleet)
railcars.description: The B Cars were ordered in the 1990s to expand the fleet for increased ridership. They featured updated electronics and improved climate control systems.

railcars.name: C Car (C1/C2)
railcars.description: The C Cars were the last vehicles to use the original BART car design. They introduced improved accessibility features and updated passenger information displays.

railcars.name: Fleet of the Future
railcars.description: The Fleet of the Future represents a complete modernization of BART's rolling stock. These cars feature a new interior design with wider aisles, digital displays, LED lighting, and improved ventilation. The entire legacy fleet is being replaced by these new vehicles.

railcars.name: Oakland Airport Connector
railcars.description: The Oakland Airport Connector uses automated cable-driven vehicles to connect the Coliseum BART station to Oakland International Airport. The system operates without on-board operators.
